reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes joining Forsage through paid slots and coordinated teams, presenting a new blockchain launch as a chance to enter early and benefit from participant activity. The speaker highlights claims that participants earned tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars or became millionaires, urges viewers to prepare teams and wallets, and creates urgency by saying not to miss the upcoming launch. This is a recruitment-dependent earning solicitation rather than neutral reporting or an ordinary wallet tutorial.

opening.argument: The presentation contains meaningful uncertainty rather than a guaranteed promise. The speaker concedes that a solution for Ethereum is not under his control and that its timing is unknown, while describing the new launch as a response to network problems and transaction fees. That framing supports viewing the message as a conditional business update: participation may be attractive if the technical issues persist, but the speaker does not promise that any viewer will profit. The claim about earlier participants is presented as historical context, not as a guaranteed result for everyone. The evidence therefore leaves room for a cautious market-commentary interpretation rather than establishing deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: But we don't know when this will happen. It is not depend on us.
The fees on Ethereum are too huge.
Many participants earned tens of thousands and hundreds of thousands of dollars and some even became dollar millionaires in Forsage.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats promotional language as proof of deception, but “before your teams” describes anticipated timing within the speaker’s proposed structure, not a guaranteed return. Likewise, “do not miss this moment” is ordinary launch enthusiasm and does not state a deadline, guaranteed income, or inevitable success. The earnings statement also says that some participants earned money, not that every viewer will.

citations.quote: You need to be there before your teams.

Many participants earned tens of thousands and hundreds of thousands of dollars and some even became dollar millionaires in Forsage.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Uncertainty about when network problems will be fixed does not caution viewers about losing money or make the opportunity non-soliciting. The speaker immediately converts that uncertainty into a reason to join a new blockchain, says participants will pursue all platforms to avoid missing payments, and urges preparation. Saying that some people earned large amounts still supplies an attractive profit narrative without substantiation.

opening.argument: The video can be read as an operational and technology update about deploying a program across blockchains. It discusses network congestion, fees, bandwidth, contract testing, supported wallets, and how to switch a wallet to Binance Smart Chain. It also explains the planned sequence for releasing X3, X4, and XGold. Those are concrete implementation details that resemble a product demonstration or technical briefing. The accompanying visual material includes a market chart, reinforcing a financial-technology commentary context. Although the speaker is enthusiastic, the central subject can be understood as how the platform and its infrastructure are being expanded.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material promotional does not eliminate its substantial technical content. The discussion explains why the network is being selected, what contracts will launch first, and which wallets can be configured. The reference account highlights selected persuasive phrases but does not establish that the video is only a recruitment pitch rather than an explanation of a blockchain rollout.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical details describe how to participate; they do not change the purpose of the invitation. The speaker tells viewers to prepare teams and wallets, obtain BNB, and enter before their teams. The contract and wallet explanation is therefore operational guidance attached to a recruitment and payment structure, not neutral education detached from participation.

opening.argument: The message can be framed as promotion of access to a software-based blockchain program with disclosed entry amounts and ordinary setup instructions. It identifies the payment currency, gives the general registration amount, explains that slots have different prices, and tells users how to obtain the currency and configure compatible wallets. That is more concrete than a vague promise of free money. The supplied frames show a speaker explaining the subject and a separate market-chart display, but do not show a wallet address, a completed transaction, or a specific payout. On this record, the evidence does not itself establish a guaranteed return or a completed deceptive transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference account calls the slots and teams a scam mechanism, but the quoted material still does not prove that any viewer was guaranteed a return or that the speaker concealed the stated entry pricing. The invitation to prepare wallets can equally accompany a legitimate software or token launch. Describing anticipated payments is not, by itself, proof that a transaction occurred or that the service was deceptive.

The absence of a shown wallet address or completed transaction is immaterial because the video is soliciting preparation and entry, not documenting a completed purchase. Its payment-dependent team structure remains central.
